result.rationale: The migration inserts the raw old setting values directly via SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and path stripping). Meanwhile `record_for_host` matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a migrated row like 'http://discourse.org' (values the old setting allowed, and which tests like `Fabricate(:embeddable_host, host: 'http://discourse.org')` show were expected) would never match, silently breaking previously-allowed embeds.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` inserts rows with `host` values taken directly from the old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` lines via raw SQL (`INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips scheme (`http://`/`https://`) and paths. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses a URL and compares `uri.host` (e.g., `discourse.org`) against `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. If the migrated row stored `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`, it will not match and `host_allowed?` will return false, breaking previously-allowed embeds after migration.
